findings.assertion: A 2023 Palacio Nacional historical retrospective places insurgent remains in the Metropolitan Cathedral from 1823, and says patriotic workers' societies requested their transfer to the San José chapel in 1895; the 17 September 1925 El Universal account also places the urns in that chapel. This is a history of successive locations, not a claim that every named insurgent passed through Cathedral.
findings.source_locator: Palacio Nacional 2023 indexed paragraph on 1823/1895; El Universal 17 Sep 1925 reprint lines 37–39
findings.limitations: Gov original 2023 article returned 403; 1823/1895 transfer minutes and Cathedral inventory absent.

findings.assertion: El Universal's 2019 framing says the Column's interior was modified in 1923 to make niches for urns later brought in 1925. The building's use as a funerary mausoleum therefore postdates the 1910 dedication and should not be described as part of the architect's original inauguration.
findings.source_locator: El Universal 2019 reporter introduction lines 21–27; 2017 INBAL technical bulletin separate earlier batch
findings.limitations: 1923 adaptation date is reporter narrative, not 1923 building-plan primary evidence; label a lead not a verified construction date.

findings.assertion: The 17 September 1925 newspaper's retrospective of the previous day's ceremony describes a procession from the Metropolitan Cathedral to the Column of Independence that took about one hour and ended with a 21-gun salute. The reported duration is a period witness's ceremonial journey, not a modern walk time.
findings.source_locator: El Universal 17 Sep 1925 reproduced passages lines 50–58
findings.limitations: Original 1925 page facsimile has not been collated in full; street-by-street 1925 route not verified and must not be inferred.

findings.assertion: The 1925 newspaper describes spectators on Reforma balconies—especially women—throwing flowers over the passing urns, and soldiers honoring the cortege along the avenue. The report supports a history of civilian participation that is distinct from the state’s formal military arrangements.
findings.limitations: A single contemporary journalist's language does not establish a demographic count or public unanimity.

findings.assertion: The 17 September 1925 newspaper explicitly questioned whether a cranium attributed to José María Morelos might instead be that of Francisco Xavier Mina or Pedro Moreno. This is evidence of contemporary uncertainty about relic identification, not evidence identifying any person's remains.
findings.source_locator: El Universal 1925 reproduced 'Cómo quedaron los restos' lines 43–48
findings.limitations: Do not resolve biological identity from a journalist's uncertainty; full chain of custody, forensic and INAH archives required.

findings.assertion: A contemporary 1925 report describes President Plutarco Elías Calles lifting the lid of an urn attributed to Miguel Hidalgo and placing inside a card bearing his signature, date and time. This is a specific presidential gesture reported at the time, not independently verified inventory evidence.
findings.limitations: Locate the contemporary issue scan or photographed card/inventory before treating as materially corroborated.

findings.assertion: The newspaper records bronze niche closures, presidential and diplomatic wreaths, roughly fifty floral wreaths, and temporary public access to view the crypt immediately after the 1925 ceremony. Those historical access arrangements must not be offered as a claim about 2026 visitor access.
findings.limitations: Single paper's report; current crypt access and surviving original wreaths/bronze plaques unverified.

findings.assertion: The 2020 Secretaría de Cultura retrospective distinguishes Leona Vicario's reburial history from the story of remains held in Cathedral: it reports her transfer with Andrés Quintana Roo from Santa Paula to the Rotonda de las Personas Ilustres in 1900, followed by her removal to the Column in 1925. Thus an undifferentiated 'all came from Cathedral' account would be inaccurate.
findings.source_locator: Secretaría de Cultura 23 Jan 2020 indexed article, paragraphs on 28 May 1900 and 1925; full text 403
findings.limitations: Specific Rotonda and niche details are excerpt-only; cemetery inventories and 1925 transfer list not inspected.

findings.assertion: An official 16 August 2010 Secretaría de Cultura release reports INAH physical-anthropology reviewers identifying a historical omission: 1925 door inscriptions named twelve insurgents, whereas officials then assessed remains of fourteen, with Pedro Moreno and Víctor Rosales absent from the inscriptions. This reports the institution's 2010 conclusion, not final independent forensic proof of identification.
findings.limitations: Original osteological report, inscription images before/after, and chain-of-custody records not inspected.

findings.assertion: The 2010 government account describes conservation work on the insurgents' remains in two stages, remineralization and consolidation, and a plan for controlled humidity and temperature. It also says a July 2011 return and inscription correction were intended—neither actual completion nor present conditions are established by this prospective release.
findings.limitations: 2010 press summary not technical conservation report; proposed 2011 completion must be verified against completion records.

findings.assertion: The August 2010 transfer procession with fourteen urns traveled from Chapultepec along Reforma, Avenida Juárez, Eje Central and Cinco de Mayo to the Zócalo and Palacio Nacional, according to the contemporary government release. This is a different 2010 route and ceremonial context from the 1925 Cathedral-to-Column procession and must not be conflated in a historical walk.
findings.limitations: The 2010 published route is a government account and not route geometry for a 1925 procession.
